payload.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

ambiguities: The ambient ring for the congruence is not specified, so it is unclear whether the statement is meant as a polynomial congruence or a congruence after clearing denominators in a rational-function ring.
The term q to the power k(d minus d k minus 2r) divided by 2 may require half-integer powers of q, but the statement does not say whether such powers are allowed.
The notation is defined for generic parameters a, b, and c, but their algebraic domain is not explicitly stated.
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The q-Pochhammer symbol with k = 0 is understood to be 1 as an empty product.
The cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(q) is taken in its standard meaning for positive integer n.
The congruence is intended in an algebraic setting where the displayed expression is defined, likely a polynomial or localized rational-function ring in q.
The exponent involving division by 2 suggests that the intended ambient ring may allow half-integer powers of q, or else the exponent is implicitly integral in the intended setting.

domain_restrictions: q is treated as a formal indeterminate.
m is an integer parameter in the q-integer definition.
a, b, and c are formal parameters in the q-shifted factorial notation.
j is an integer index running from 0 to k minus 1 in the product defining the q-shifted factorial.
k is a nonnegative integer in the notation definitions and a summation index from 0 to n minus 1 in the theorem.
d and r are positive integers.
r is less than or equal to d.
n is an integer greater than 1.
The modulus is the product of the q-integer [n]_q and the square of the nth cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(q).
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r less than or equal to d, and every integer n greater than 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the finite sum from k = 0 to n minus 1 of the term [3 d k plus r]_q times (q^r, q^r, q^d; q^(2d))_k times (q^d; q^d)_k squared times q to the power k(d minus d k minus 2r) divided by 2, all divided by (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k, is congruent modulo [n]_q times Phi_n(q)^2 to [r n]_q times q to the power r(1 minus n) divided by 2.
quantifier_order: For the notation, define the q-integer and q-shifted factorials for arbitrary formal parameters q, m, a, b, c, with k a nonnegative integer and j ranging from 0 to k minus 1.
For all positive integers d and r such that gcd(d, r) = 1 and r is less than or equal to d.
For every integer n greater than 1 such that n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
For the finite sum over k from 0 to n minus 1, the congruence statement holds.

result_payload.statement_nl_received: Define q-integer [m]_q as (1 minus q^m) divided by (1 minus q), define q-shifted factorial (a; q)_k as the product over j from 0 to k minus 1 of (1 minus a q^j), define (a, b, c; q)_k as the product of (a; q)_k, (b; q)_k, and (c; q)_k, and let Phi_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r less than or equal to d, and for every integer n greater than 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the sum from k = 0 to n minus 1 of [3dk + r]_q times (q^r, q^r, q^d; q^(2d))_k times (q^d; q^d)_k squared times q to the power k(d minus dk minus 2r) divided by 2, all divided by (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k, is congruent modulo [n]_q times Phi_n(q)^2 to [rn]_q times q to the power r(1 minus n) divided by 2.
